title: Proper modification transfer without an amplitude claim
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y,S$ be schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to S$ and $\pi:Y\to X$ be proper $k$-morphisms,
and suppose $\pi$ is an isomorphism over the open $U\subset X$.
Let $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ have the reduced closed
structure. If $\mathcal C(f\pi)$ and $\mathcal C(fi)$ hold,
then $\mathcal C(f)$ holds, with the coefficient and sheaf conventions of
[def-finrepair-property-c] and the morphism conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: Work throughout with the fixed finite ring $\Lambda$ and small etale module sheaves of [def-finrepair-property-c]. The inherited coefficient convention fixes a positive integer $N$ annihilating $\Lambda$ and invertible on the schemes; inverse images to $U$, $Z$ and $U'$  preserve invertibility. The ring $\Lambda$ is Noetherian because its finite set of ideals admits no infinite strictly ascending chain. Fix a constructible $F$ on $X$ and put $G=j^{-1}F$, $H=i^{-1}F$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. By [prop-constructible-pullback], $G$ and $H$ are constructible. The field $k$ and the finite-type $k$-structures on $X,Y,S$ are explicit hypotheses of the corrected item, not consequences of the definition of $\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], including its module-sheaf clause, to obtain $0\to j_!G\to F\to i_*H\to0$.

Put $U'=Y\times_XU=\pi^{-1}(U)$, let $j':U'\hookrightarrow Y$ and $h:U'\to U$ be the projections, and put $G'=h^{-1}G$. The hypothesis that $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $U$ says exactly that $h$ is an isomorphism. By [prop-constructible-pullback] $G'$ is constructible; [lem-fin-extension-by-zero] makes $E=j'_!G'$ constructible on the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$. The current statement of [lem-finrepair-modification-extension-zero] applies to the finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$, the proper morphism $\pi$, the open immersion $j$ and this cartesian square. Its canonical adjunction map $a:j_!G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*E$ is an isomorphism and $R^b\pi_*E=0$ for every $b>0$. Use $a^{-1}$ for the identification $\pi_*E\simeq j_!G$ in the next step. This application needs no finiteness of the stalks of $G$ and no invertibility assumption beyond the inherited coefficient conventions fixed in step 1.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] to $Y\xrightarrow{\pi}X\xrightarrow f S$ and $E$. Its $E_2^{a,b}=R^af_*(R^b\pi_*E)$ is zero for $b>0$, and its bottom row is $A_a=R^af_*j_!G$. Since each next-page entry is a kernel modulo an image in the current entry, the positive rows remain zero by induction on the page. All differentials from page 2 onward meeting the bottom row vanish: outgoing targets have second degree $1-r<0$, incoming sources have positive second degree $r-1$. In total degree $q$ the finite abutment filtration therefore has just one nonzero graded piece, at $(q,0)$; all earlier graded pieces vanish, so $F^0=\cdots=F^q$, and $F^{q+1}=0$. Thus $R^q(f\pi)_*E\simeq A_q$. Since $E$ is constructible, $\mathcal C(f\pi)$ in [def-finrepair-property-c] proves that $A_q$ is constructible for every $q\ge0$.

proof.text: The explicit hypothesis that $X$ is of finite type over $k$ permits applying [lem-fin-closed-immersion] to constructible $H=i^{-1}F$ on $Z$. It gives $R^bi_*H=0$ for $b>0$; in degree zero the right derived functor is $i_*$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] for $Z\xrightarrow i X\xrightarrow f S$: again only the bottom row survives. For total degree $q$, outgoing differentials have negative second degree, incoming ones positive second degree, and all positive-second-degree entries stay zero on every page. The filtration therefore has zero quotients at indices $p<q$, giving $F^0=\cdots=F^q$, while $F^{q+1}=0$ and $F^q/F^{q+1}$ is the bottom-row term. Hence $B_q:=R^qf_*i_*H\simeq R^q(fi)_*H$. The hypothesis $\mathcal C(fi)$, applied to constructible $H$, makes every $B_q$ constructible by [def-finrepair-property-c]. This uses the stated vanishing of the closed-immersion node, not an unstated exactness clause.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the short exact sequence of step 1 and $f_*$. Its source and target are abelian module-sheaf categories, its source has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $f_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Thus for $q>0$ there is an exact segment $B_{q-1}\to A_q\to R^qf_*F\to B_q\to A_{q+1}$. For $q=0$ the sequence starts $0\to A_0\to f_*F\to B_0\to A_1$.

proof.text: Set $B_{-1}=0$. Exactness in step 5 identifies the image of $A_q\to R^qf_*F$ with $C_q=\operatorname{coker}(B_{q-1}\to A_q)$ and the image of $R^qf_*F\to B_q$ with $K_q=\ker(B_q\to A_{q+1})$. Factoring through these images gives $0\to C_q\to R^qf_*F\to K_q\to0$. For $q=0$ this reads $C_0=A_0$, using the initial injectivity, so no negative derived functor is required.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph, displayed short exact sequence

proof.text: The terms $A_q$, $A_{q+1}$, $B_q$ and, for $q>0$, $B_{q-1}$ are constructible by steps 3-4. By the kernel and cokernel clauses of [thm-constructible-serre], $C_q$ and $K_q$ are constructible (for $q=0$, $C_0=A_0$). Its extension clause applied to step 6 proves $R^qf_*F$ constructible. Since $F$ and $q\ge0$ were arbitrary, this is $\mathcal C(f)$ by [def-finrepair-property-c]. No uniform bound on $q$ or vanishing assertion has been used.
